items.h: Bhayshul Tuten (ankle/foot) will practice Friday
items.s: Bhayshul Tuten (ankle/foot) will practice for the first time this week on Friday. Tuten has been dealing with ankle and foot issues going back to last week. He ended up playing last Thursday against the Ravens, going for 29 yards and a score on 12 carries. Tuten seems likely to play against the Titans on Sunday too, but his workload could be limited once again.

items.h: Will practice Friday
items.s: Tuten (ankle/foot) will practice Friday, Ryan O'Halloran of The Florida Times-Union reports. Tuten was unable to practice both Wednesday and Thursday, but head coach Liam Coen revealed that he will be back out there Friday. It won't be clear until after practice if Tuten practiced fully or on a limited basis, but his participation alone bodes well for his chances of suiting up Sunday against the Titans.

items.h: Bhayshul Tuten "Good to Go" for Sunday Against Titans
items.s: Jacksonville Jaguars running back Bhayshul Tuten (ankle/foot) is expected to play Sunday against Tennessee. Head coach Liam Coen said Friday that Tuten will be "good to go" after missing practice Wednesday and Thursday. The rookie played through the injuries in last week's win over Baltimore, rushing 12 times for 29 yards and a touchdown. He played just 36% of the offensive snaps, with Chris Rodriguez Jr. handling additional work. Coen's comments are encouraging for Tuten's Week 10 availability, though his workload remains worth watching after last week's reduced playing time. Rodriguez (hand) is also dealing with an injury, which could affect Jacksonville's backfield rotation against the…

items.h: Bhayshul Tuten (ankle/foot) doesn't practice again Thursday
items.s: Bhayshul Tuten (ankle/foot) did not take part in Jacksonville's practice again on Thursday. Tuten has now missed both of Jacksonville's practices to start the week. Friday's injury report should give us some clarity on if he's trending to play on Sunday or not, but either way fantasy managers should be preparing for the possibility that he will be sidelined or limited in Week 10, especially with Jacksonville likely not needing him in an easy matchup against the Titans this week.

items.h: Sits out another practice
items.s: Tuten (ankle/foot) didn't practice Thursday. Tuten didn't practice Wednesday either, though as Mia O'Brien of 1010 XL 92.5 FM Jacksonville points out, Tuten logged 'DNPs' Monday through Wednesday last week yet still played in last Thursday's win over the Ravens. In any case, Friday's practice report will reveal whether Tuten is able to work at all this week, as well as his game status for Sunday's game against the Titans. Next up for carries if he ends up sidelined this weekend is Chris Rodriguez (hand), who was limited Thursday.

items.h: Spotted without helmet Thursday
items.s: Tuten (ankle/foot) was the Jaguars' only player without a helmet during the initial portion of Thursday's practice, Ryan O'Halloran of The Florida Times-Union reports. Tuten was deemed a non-participant in practice Wednesday, but his presence on the field a day later suggests that he could advance to limited participation Thursday. In any case, the Jaguars' next practice report will clarify that, as well as how much work fellow RB Chris Rodriguez (hand) got in.

items.h: Bhayshul Tuten (ankle/foot) misses practice Wednesday
items.s: Bhayshul Tuten did not practice on Wednesday. Tuten misses practice to start the week after a mini bye. He will need to be monitored in practice on Thursday and Friday.

items.h: Bhayshul Tuten Misses Practice on Wednesday
items.s: Jacksonville Jaguars running back Bhayshul Tuten (ankle, foot) was listed as a non-participant in Wednesday's practice, according to Ryan O'Halloran of The Florida Times-Union. Tuten was a game-time decision for last Thursday's win over the Baltimore Ravens, but he ultimately was active. However, he played a season-low 36% of the offensive snaps and tied a season low with 12 rushing attempts for only 29 yards. He did not have a target in the passing game for the first time all year, but he somewhat salvaged his fantasy day with his fourth rushing touchdown of the season. The 23-year-old's status is once again up in the air for the Jaguars' Week 10 divisional clash against the Tennessee…

items.h: Logs 'DNP' on Wednesday
items.s: Tuten (ankle/foot) was listed as a non-participant in practice Wednesday, Ryan O'Halloran of The Florida Times-Union reports. It remains to be seen if Tuten is simply managing a couple of aches and pains in the wake of Week 9 action or is in danger of missing the Jaguars' next game, so his status is worth tracking ahead of Sunday's game against the Titans. Fellow RB Chris Rodriguez also appeared on Wednesday's injury report after being deemed limited by a hand injury.

items.h: Bhayshul Tuten Eyes More in Week 10 After Extra Time Off
items.s: Jacksonville running back Bhayshul Tuten battled ankle and foot injuries going into Week 9, but after playing on Thursday, he had some extra time to heal, so he should be able to take on more in Week 10 and beyond. He only played 20 offensive snaps in Week 9 against Baltimore - that was 35.7% of the team's total, which was his lowest mark of the season, but it also came in a lopsided game. Tuten still had a rushing touchdown and 29 yards across 12 carries. He's been a pretty solid fantasy option this season, with 521 rushing yards and four touchdowns over 122 carries, plus has caught 15 of his 16 targets for 181 yards and three more scores. Fantasy owners should expect more good showings…

items.h: Bhayshul Tuten struggles in rainy game
items.s: Bhayshul Tuten ran 12 times for 29 yards and a touchdown in the Jaguars' 33-10 win over the Ravens on Thursday. Tuten struggled to get much going in this game, with his longest run being six yards. The Ravens' defense did a good job keeping things in front of them and not allowing many explosive plays by the Jags, and Tuten suffered for it. He will look to have a better time out against the Titans next week.

items.h: Scores TD in Week 9 win
items.s: Tuten (ankle/foot) rushed 12 times for 29 yards and a touchdown in the Jaguars' 33-10 win over the Ravens on Thursday night. Tuten fought through the pair of lower-body injuries that made him a game-time decision, recording his fourth rushing touchdown of the campaign on a one-yard run to cap off the opening possession of the contest. The second-year back had to grind for every yard he got on the ground, but fortunately for Tuten, the Jaguars built a comfortable enough lead where he was able to benefit from an early end to his night. Tuten has now scored in back-to-back games, and he'll have some extra time to get healthier ahead of a Week 10 road matchup against the Titans on Sunday, Nov.…

Bhayshul Tuten Finds End Zone While Battling Injuries
items.s: Jacksonville Jaguars running back Bhayshul Tuten rushed for 29 yards and a touchdown on 12 carries in his team's 33-10 win against the hosting Baltimore Ravens on Thursday Night Football. Tuten came into this one nursing a foot and ankle injury that caused him to log three straight DNPs in preparation for Week 9's clash, so it's no surprise to see him post his worst output of the campaign despite scoring his seventh all-purpose touchdown. The Virginia Tech product saw his last touch of the contest with 3:02 remaining in the third quarter, as backfield mates Chris Rodriguez Jr. and Ameer Abdullah salted away the clock over the final frame. It may not be the results fantasy managers were…

items.h: Bhayshul Tuten (ankle) active for Thursday Night Football
items.s: Bhayshul Tuten (ankle) is active for the Jaguars Thursday Night Football contest against the Ravens. Fire up the Jaguars RB1, who has been on a hot streak coming into this game and should have ample opportunity to put up points in what should be a blowout.

items.h: Officially active versus Baltimore
items.s: Tuten (ankle/foot) officially is listed as active for Thursday night's game against the Ravens. It was previously reported that Tuten, who was viewed as a game-time decision for the contest, would be good to go, and now that has been confirmed. Assuming no in-game limitations or setbacks, Tuten is in line to continue to lead the Jaguars backfield in Week 9. If, however, his reps end up being managed at all, added touches could be available for Chris Rodriguez, Ameer Abdullah and LeQuint Allen. When healthy, Tuten has maintained steady volume through seven games, averaging 15.7 carries and 70.3 rushing yards with three rushing scores, while also having recorded a 15-181-3 receiving line in…

items.h: In line to play Thursday
items.s: Tuten (ankle) is on track to play in Thursday night's game against the Ravens, after going through what Jeremy Fowler of ESPN.com describes as an extensive pregame workout. Tuten, who was listed as a DNP on all three of the Jaguars' Week 9 injury reports, was viewed as a game-time decision for Thursday's contest, but it looks like the running back will give it a go after all. Official confirmation of his status will arrive, either way, once the Jaguars' inactives are posted ahead of the team's 8:15 p.m. ET kickoff.

items.h: Bhayshul Tuten (ankle) should be good to go for TNF
items.s: Bhayshul Tuten (ankle) should be good to go for TNF barring a pregame setback. Tuten looked fine durinf his final touches on Sunday, but practice reports didn't look especially promising at first. However, his status has improved and it sounds like he will be active for Thursday. Start him if he's active.

items.h: Expected to play Thursday
items.s: Tuten (ankle/foot) "should be" available for Thursday night's game against the Ravens barring any pregame setbacks, Jeremy Fowler of ESPN reports. Tuten logged DNP listings on all three of the Jaguars' Week 9 injury reports ahead of the contest and had been considered a game-time decision. Fowler's report indicates that the running back is trending toward active status, but those considering Tuten in Week 9 fantasy lineups nonetheless will want to verify his playing status ahead of Thursday's 8:15 p.m. ET kickoff.

items.h: Bhayshul Tuten Will Play Thursday, Plans to "Let it Rip"
items.s: Jacksonville Jaguars running back Bhayshul Tuten (ankle) is good to go and will be active on Thursday night against the Baltimore Ravens after going through a pre-game workout, according to Ian Rapoport of the NFL Network. Tuten went through an extensive pre-game workout and plans to "let it rip," according to ESPN's Jeremy Fowler. The 23-year-old had a career-best day in the Week 8 blowout win over the division-rival Indianapolis Colts on Sunday, recording 104 rushing yards and a touchdown on 16 carries while adding 55 receiving yards and another score on two receptions, but he came out of that contest with an ankle injury that made him a game-time decision for Thursday's Week 9 tilt in…

The 23-year-old was held out of practice on the short week while he battles an ankle/foot issue, but it appears he is gearing up to play on Thursday night. He's also played some of his best football lately, logging 246 yards from scrimmage and four touchdowns over the last two weeks. As long as Tuten is…

items.h: Bhayshul Tuten a Borderline RB1 if Healthy Against Ravens
items.s: Jacksonville Jaguars running back Bhayshul Tuten (ankle/foot) will be a great fantasy option once more in Week 9 against the Baltimore Ravens as long as he can play. He has not practiced all week and is currently listed as questionable. If he isn't able to play, backup Chris Rodriguez Jr. should be in line for most of the work. The young back is coming off back-to-back great performances, combining for four touchdowns and 246 total yards. Tuten has received consistent volume all season and is starting to raise his upside through more receiving work and finding the end zone more. The Ravens do rank sixth against running backs in fantasy, so there is a chance a hurt Tuten doesn't do as well…

items.h: Bhayshul Tuten (ankle/foot) officially questionable for Thursday
items.s: Bhayshul Tuten (ankle/foot) is officially questionable for Thursday night's game against the Baltimore Ravens. Tuten wasn't able to practice all week due to an ankle/foot issue that he's dealing with, and now he is officially considered questionable to play on Thursday night because of it. It sounds like he is expected to be a game-time decision, so fantasy managers should keep close tabs on updates about his status leading up to kickoff and should have a good backup option in place in case he's out.

items.h: Questionable for Thursday after no practice
items.s: Tuten (ankle/foot) is listed questionable for Thursday's game against the Ravens. For the third day in a row, Tuten went down as a non-participant on the Jaguars' injury report, even though head coach Liam Coen suggested the running back would practice in a limited fashion Wednesday, per Cameron Wolfe of NFL Network. The coach added that the Jaguars will be viewing Tuten as a game-time decision for Thursday's tilt, with his availability perhaps hinging on how he fares during a gameday workout. If Tuten ends up missing his first game of the season or is active but available in only a limited capacity, Chris Rodriguez would be in store for a larger role out of the backfield.

items.h: Bhayshul Tuten (foot) could be game-time decision Thursday
items.s: Jaguars head coach Liam Coen said Bhayshul Tuten could be a game-time decision for Thursday's game against the Ravens. Tuten will need to be monitored closer to kickoff on Thursday. Chris Rodriguez would be next up if he is sidelined.

items.h: Trending toward game-time call Thursday
items.s: Jaguars head coach Liam Coen said Wednesday that Tuten (ankle/foot) is feeling better, but the running back's status for Thursday's contest versus the Ravens is expected to come down to a game-time decision, John Shipley of SI.com reports. Tuten was listed as a non-participant on the Jaguars' first two Week 9 practice reports, but he may be in line to take some reps during Wednesday's session. The 23-year-old looks poised to take a questionable tag into the team's matchup with Baltimore, but if he fares well in practice Wednesday and while working out early Thursday, he could get the green light to play on a short week. If Tuten suits up, it's conceivable that he handles a lighter workload…

items.s: Jacksonville Jaguars running back Bhayshul Tuten (ankle, foot) is listed as questionable for Thursday night's Week 9 matchup against the Baltimore Ravens, according to Ryan O'Halloran. Tuten did not participate in practice throughout the short week, including Monday's estimated session, leaving his availability uncertain despite head coach Liam Coen indicating on Wednesday that he was feeling better. The 23-year-old is coming off his best performance of the season, rushing for 104 yards and a touchdown on 16 carries while adding two receptions for 55 yards and another score against Indianapolis. items.h: Bhayshul Tuten Still Not Practicing Wednesday
items.s: Jacksonville Jaguars running back Bhayshul Tuten (ankle), fresh off his first career 100-yard performance, was not spotted during the media-accessible portion of Wednesday's practice, marking his third absence of the week. The Jaguars face the Ravens on Thursday night, and Tuten's ankle injury, paired with a short week of preparation, has cast doubt on his availability and made him a potential game-time decision. Accounting for four touchdowns in his last two games, Tuten is the fantasy RB1 by points per game since Week 6. If the second-year back is unable to suit up on Thursday, Chris Rodriguez Jr., who scored a 28-yard touchdown of his own in Week 8, becomes a viable starting candidate…

Head coach Liam Coen offered the update after Tuten missed Tuesday's practice and was listed as a nonparticipant on Monday's estimated injury report. The 23-year-old is coming off his best performance of the season, totaling 159 scrimmage yards and two touchdowns on 18 touches against Indianapolis in Week 8. items.h: Bhayshul Tuten (foot) officially misses practice Tuesday
items.s: Bhayshul Tuten did not practice on Tuesday. Tuten opens the week with back-to-back missed practices. His status will need to be monitored closely on Wednesday.

items.h: Sits out Tuesday's practice
items.s: The Jaguars listed Tuten (ankle/foot) as a non-participant in Tuesday's practice. For the second day in a row, Tuten went down as a non-participant on Jacksonville's Week 9 injury report while he nurses a pair of lower-body injuries coming out of this past Sunday's win over the Colts. If Tuten can get back on the field in some capacity Wednesday, it would put him in a good spot to play Thursday against the Ravens. However, if Tuten fails to practice and is ultimately ruled out for Thursday, Chris Rodriguez (hand) -- who has been a limited practice participant so far this week -- would be the top candidate to lead Jacksonville's ground attack in Baltimore.

items.h: Bhayshul Tuten (foot) not practicing Tuesday
items.s: Bhayshul Tuten was not seen practicing on Tuesday. Tuten was also listed as a DNP on Monday. With Jacksonville playing on Thursday, he'll likely have to practice in some capacity on Wednesday.

items.h: Not spotted at practice
items.s: Tuten (ankle/foot) was not spotted during the portion of Tuesday's practice open to the media, according to Michael DiRocco of ESPN.com. Tuten was listed as a non-participant on Monday's estimated injury report on a day the Jaguars did not practice, and although the Jaguars will return to the field Tuesday, it appears Tuten will not due to the lower-leg injuries. Tuten will not have much time to get any work in this week with the Jaguars facing the Ravens on Thursday, and if he is unable to go the door will be opened for Chris Rodriguez (hand), LeQuint Allen and Ameer Abdullah.

items.s: Jacksonville Jaguars running back Bhayshul Tuten (foot) ran for a career-high 104 yards in a Week 8 blowout win over the Colts, but with a short week of preparation ahead of a Thursday night matchup with the Ravens, he was not spotted during the media-accessible portion of Tuesday's practice. Tuten missed Monday's practice with the foot and ankle injury suffered in Sunday's win, and as the only player not spotted on Tuesday, he is trending toward his first missed game of the year. Tuten has scored four touchdowns in his last two games, ranking as the overall RB1 by points per game over that stretch, but his absence would create an opportunity for Chris Rodriguez Jr., who scored a 28-yard…

items.h: Dealing with ankle, foot injuries
items.s: Tuten was a non-participant at Monday's walkthrough due to ankle and foot injuries. Tuten is coming off a sterling performance Sunday against the Colts in which he reeled off 159 yards from scrimmage and two total TDs on 18 touches, but he now has a pair of health concerns in tow. The Jaguars may be exercising caution with their No. 1 RB, but his status -- along with backup Chris Rodriguez (hand), who was listed as limited -- will be watched to get a sense of who may be available to the backfield Thursday at Baltimore.

items.h: Bhayshul Tuten Misses Monday's Practice With Multiple Injuries
items.s: Jacksonville Jaguars running back Bhayshul Tuten (ankle, foot) was a non-participant during Monday's walkthrough, per Travis D. Holmes. Tuten is coming off an epic performance against the Indianapolis Colts on Sunday. He carried the ball 16 times for 104 yards and a touchdown. He also hauled in two receptions for 55 receiving yards and an additional score through the air. It appears that Tuten picked up a minor injury during that game, but fantasy managers shouldn't be too worried right now. There's still plenty of time for Tuten to get ready in time for Thursday's Week 9 matchup against the Baltimore Ravens. Fantasy managers should continue monitoring Tuten's status throughout the week.

items.h: Bhayshul Tuten gashes Colts in Week 8 rout
items.s: Bhayshul Tuten went for 104 yards and a touchdown on 16 carries, adding in two receptions for 55 yards and another score in Sunday's 42-7 blowout of the Colts. Tuten turned in the first 100-yard rushing performance of his career on Sunday while also setting a new personal best in receiving yards. The second-year speedster has now scored twice in both of the Jaguars' last two games and is up to six total touchdowns - three rushing, three receiving - for the campaign. Tuten is quickly inserting himself among the league's most potent dual-threat weapons at his position, as he's averaging nearly 18 touches and over 96 yards of offense per game.

Tuten is up to 4.5 yards per carry after averaging a season-best 6.5 yards per tote Sunday, and he's added six total touchdowns heading into a Week 9 road…

Bhayshul Tuten Continues Breakout Season with Dominant Week 8 Showing
items.s: Jacksonville Jaguars running back Bhayshul Tuten dominated in his team's 42-7 Week 8 win over the Indianapolis Colts, recording 16 carries for 104 yards and a touchdown, and hauling in two catches for 55 yards and an additional score. Tuten has been very consistent in 2026, recording at least 87 yards from scrimmage in five out of six games heading into Week 8. The star production is starting to follow now as well, as he's logged two touchdowns in consecutive games. Between Tuten's ability to make explosive plays as both a rusher and a receiver and Jacksonville's potent offensive attack, the 23-year-old profiles as a must-start running back heading into the Jaguars' Week 9 showdown against…

Bhayshul Tuten in Line for Second Straight Big Performance in Week 8
items.s: Jacksonville Jaguars running back Bhayshul Tuten is coming off his best fantasy performance of the season as he heads into a Week 8 matchup with the Indianapolis Colts. He has been a model of consistency so far, putting up 65-plus rushing yards in his first five games. He had his worst rushing output of the season in Week 6 and the fewest carries, totaling just 39 rushing yards on 12 carries, but countered that with his best receiving game of the season. Overall, Tuten finished with 87 scrimmage yards, 16 total touches, and two receiving touchdowns. Coming off a Week 7 bye and heading into a matchup with the 22nd-ranked defense against running backs in fantasy means fantasy managers have…

items.h: Bhayshul Tuten Has Topped 85 Scrimmage Yards Four Games Running
items.s: Jacksonville Jaguars running back Bhayshul Tuten has surpassed 85 scrimmage yards in four consecutive games as the team's lead back, accumulating 388 rushing yards, 126 receiving yards and four touchdowns through six appearances. Coming off Jacksonville's Week 7 bye, the second-year back remains a strong RB2 option in 12-team leagues against the Indianapolis Colts, with his growing receiving involvement adding to his fantasy appeal. He caught all four targets for 48 yards and two touchdowns against the Houston Texans in Week 6 after averaging just two targets per game through the first five weeks, an increased involvement in the passing game that is particularly encouraging for PPR…

items.h: Bhayshul Tuten hits pay dirt twice in Week 6 loss
items.s: Bhayshul Tuten rushed for 39 yards on 12 carries in the 34-31 loss to the Texans. He caught 5-of-7 targets for 48 yards and two touchdowns. Tuten did have a rushing touchdown called back on a holding call, limiting his rushing output. His two touchdowns receptions marked his first receiving touchdowns of the season, and is a good sign for him being more involved in the passing game in the future. Tuten and the Jaguars will head to the bye in Week 7.

items.h: Two receiving TDs in Week 6 loss
items.s: Tuten carried the ball 12 times for 39 yards and caught all four of his targets for 48 yards and two touchdowns in Sunday's 34-31 loss to the Texans. While the Houston front seven kept him bottled up on the ground -- Tuten's longest run went for just five yards -- the second-year RB made an impact through the air, turning a dump pass from Trevor Lawrence into a 27-yard score in the second quarter before catching another two-yard TD before halftime. The receiving touchdowns were his first of the season and tied his total from all of 2025, and Tuten topped 80 scrimmage yards for the fourth straight game. The Jaguars will get a bye before facing the Colts in Week 8.

items.h: Bhayshul Tuten Adds Two Receiving Touchdowns in Week 6 Loss
items.s: Jacksonville Jaguars running back Bhayshul Tuten had 12 carries for 39 yards and added four catches for 48 yards and two receiving touchdowns in his team's loss to the Houston Texans in London. Despite being held to under 50 rushing yards for the first time this season, the 2025 fourth-round draft pick is building his reputation as a multi-faceted fantasy asset. Tuten hasn't broken out just yet, but fantasy managers should keep an eye on him after battling through a tough matchup against Houston. RotoBaller listed Tuten at RB19 in the positional rankings.

items.h: Bhayshul Tuten Taking on a Substantially Larger Workload
items.s: Jacksonville Jaguars running back Bhayshul Tuten has ascended into an enormous role in the backfield, averaging 20 touches per game over the last three weeks. He has at least 9.8 points in PPR leagues in every game this year, and he ranks as the overall RB17 so far. While Tuten's ceiling hasn't been very impressive, he has maintained a high floor while operating as a consistent RB2 option in fantasy football. Most importantly, his ascension has led to a massive decrease in volume for Chris Rodriguez Jr. Once viewed as a candidate to split touches with Tuten, Rodriguez saw his snap share drop to 13% last week as he handled just two rushing attempts. As long as Tuten is healthy, he is going…

items.h: Bhayshul Tuten approaches 100 yards of total offense Sunday
items.s: Bhayshul Tuten rushed for 72 yards on 22 carries, adding two receptions for 24 yards in Sunday's 19-17 win over the Eagles. Tuten continues to prove he can shoulder the load out of the Jaguars' backfield. The second-year pro only averaged 3.3 yards on his career-high 22 carries Sunday, but he seemed to run stronger as the game progressed. For the season, Tuten is averaging 70 yards on more than 16 carries per game with a couple of touchdowns. He's a solid RB2 with upside in most fantasy formats.

items.h: Tops 90 scrimmage yards against Philly
items.s: Tuten carried the ball 22 times for 72 yards and caught two of three targets for 24 yards in Sunday's 19-17 win over the Eagles. The second-year back set new season highs in touches and scrimmage yards as he reached 90 in the latter category for a third straight game. Tuten has yet to have a truly huge performance this season, but he's been very steady so far as the Jaguars' No. 1 RB, collecting 349 rushing yards and two TDs on 4.3 yards per carry while adding a 9-78-0 line on 10 targets through five games. Tuten hasn't gotten into the end zone in two straight games, a streak he'll look to snap in Week 6 against the Texans.

items.h: Bhayshul Tuten Could Be on the Verge of a Breakout Season
items.s: Across four games so far in 2026, Jacksonville Jaguars running back Bhayshul Tuten has recorded 60 carries for 277 yards and two touchdowns. Tuten has split rushing work to some degree with fellow Jaguars back Chris Rodriguez Jr., who has tallied 108 rushing yards and two touchdowns this season. However, Tuten has emerged as the clear lead back in Jacksonville in recent weeks, recording back-to-back games with at least 17 touches and 90 yards from scrimmage in Weeks 3 and 4. The 23-year-old currently ranks as the RB15 in half-PPR scoring and could only be on his way up as the season progresses. As long as Jacksonville's key offensive pieces around him stay healthy, Tuten profiles as a…

items.h: Bhayshul Tuten racks up 91 yards in win Sunday
items.s: Bhayshul Tuten rushed the ball 17 times for 73 yards and caught two passes for 18 yards in Sunday's 22-17 win over the Cincinnati Bengals. Tuten had a good game on Sunday, finishing as the team's top rusher and dominating the touches in the backfield en route to a win over the Bengals. Chris Rodriguez Jr. was the one to get into the end zone for the Jaguars, however, which was annoying for fantasy managers to see. The young running back should continue to be a worthwhile fantasy asset moving forward.

items.h: Good production with 19 touches
items.s: Tuten rushed 17 times for 73 yards and brought in both targets for 18 yards in the Jaguars' 22-17 win over the Bengals on Sunday. Tuten filled his usual role as the clear lead option in Jacksonville's ground attack with aplomb, grinding out tough yards on many of his carries and also contributing a 20-yard run. He also recorded multiple receptions for the third consecutive game, and although he saw backfield mate Chris Rodriguez score the Jaguars' only rushing touchdown of the day that came on a breakaway run from 25 yards out as opposed to in close. Tuten has at least 15 carries in three of his first four games heading into a Week 5 showdown against the Eagles in London next Sunday.

items.h: Tuten rushed 15 times for 73 yards and a touchdown and brought in both targets for 17 yards in the Jaguars' 35-6 win over the Patriots on Sunday.
items.s: Serving as the clear lead back once again, Tuten proved himself worthy of the role with a crisp performance that saw him consistently generate useful gains versus a talented Patriots front seven. He capped off his fantasy-friendly effort with his second rushing touchdown of the campaign, a one-yard run with just over eight minutes remaining to close out the scoring on the afternoon. Tuten is averaging an impressive 4.7 yards per carry and a solid 16.0 touches through three games, rendering him an appealing option in all formats heading into a Week 4 road showdown against the Bengals next…

items.h: Tuten rushed 13 times for 65 yards and a touchdown and brought in both targets for minus-3 yards in the Jaguars' 20-13 loss to the Broncos on Sunday.
items.s: Tuten worked as the Jaguars' clear lead back for the second time in as many games to open the season, even though his rushing workload was relatively modest Sunday. Tuten got into the end zone for the first time this season on a one-yard run early in the second quarter, and he was efficient overall against a high-caliber defense. Tuten figures to remain in the same role for a Week 3 home showdown against the defending AFC champion Patriots next Sunday.

items.h: Tuten rushed 15 times for 66 yards and brought in his only target for 22 yards in the Jaguars' 34-10 win over the Browns on Sunday. He also recovered a fumble.
items.s: Any questions surrounding the potential workload split in the Jaguars' ground attack were definitively answered for the time being Sunday, as Tuten put together an impressively efficient performance and outpaced backfield mate Chris Rodriguez by nine carries despite seeing his day come to an early end due to the lopsided score. Tuten was able to consistently generate productive runs, but he'll have a much stiffer test on the road against the Broncos in a Week 2 matchup next Sunday.

items.h: Tuten (illness) wasn't included on the Jaguars' first Week 1 injury report released Wednesday.
items.s: Tuten missed a practice one week ago after falling ill, but his absence from the Jaguars' first injury report of the season suggests that he's 100 percent healthy heading into Sunday's opener versus the Browns. Jaguars head coach Liam Coen hasn't revealed how he plans to divvy up the snaps among his running backs; even if Tuten ends up starting, he could wind up sharing the load on the ground with Chris Rodriguez. Third-down specialist LeQuint Allen (hip) didn't practice Wednesday and appears to be trending toward sitting out Week 1, potentially opening the door for both Tuten and Rodriguez…

items.h: Tuten (illness) did not practice Wednesday, Ryan O'Halloran of The Florida Times-Union reports.
items.s: Tuten should be fine by the time Week 1 against the Browns rolls around in 11 days. The second-year running back is expected to have a significant role in Jacksonville's backfield this season, but how this running back depth chart shakes out will be a situation to watch against Cleveland. All three of Tuten, Chris Rodriguez and LeQuint Allen (undisclosed) are likely to see snaps when healthy.

items.h: Tuten excelled as a receiver out of the backfield at Sunday's practice, per John Shipley of SI.com.
items.s: The Jaguars appear to be directing more passes Tuten's way at practice following the soft-tissue injury suffered by LeQuint Allen (undisclosed), who had been penciled in as the team's preferred backfield option in passing situations. Ameer Abdullah could take some passing-down work if he makes the team, but Tuten has more receiving upside than Chris Rodriguez, who has just six receptions in 35 career regular-season appearances. Tuten caught 10 of 14 targets for 79 yards and two touchdowns during his rookie regular season.

items.h: Tuten and Chris Rodriguez are listed as co-starters on the Jaguars' initial unofficial depth chart, Ryan O'Halloran of The Florida Times-Union reports.
items.s: Preseason depth charts can often be taken with a grain of salt, but in this case the listing aligns with the notion that the Jaguars will employ a committee approach to fill the void created by the offseason departure of Travis Etienne. Also in the mix for backfield touches is LeQuint Allen, who could factor in on third downs. Regardless of how the team's snaps and touches are distributed, Tuten figures to merit fantasy consideration right out of the gate this season.

items.h: During Friday's scrimmage, Tuten started the first drive with the Jaguars' offense with LeQuint Allen mixing in on third down, then Chris Rodriguez started the second drive before rotating with Tuten, John Shipley of…
items.s: Shipley notes that the Jaguars subsequently settled into a rotation where Tuten would open the drives, Rodriguez would come on the field when the team was within the 10-yard line, and then Allen would play all of the third downs. While this remains an ongoing job battle as Rodriguez works his way back from a foot injury, the scrimmage did at least provide some hints on how the Jaguars could approach their backfield workload come Week 1. For now, things seem to trending toward a committee approach that could result in Tuten and Rodriguez forming a 1A/1B combo, with Allen as a change-of-pace…

items.h: With Chris Rodriguez (foot) not yet ready for team drills, Tuten got the bulk of the first-team reps with the offense during Wednesday's training camp practice, John Shipley of SI.com reports.
items.s: As Shipley notes, the battle for backfield slotting between Tuten and Rodriguez will be one to monitor closely, but for now Shipley suggests that it looks like Tuten -- who looked sharp during Wednesday's session -- is taking the lead early on. That said, Rodriguez is being eased back into the mix after having undergone an offseason foot procedure, so the competition between the two figures to heat up once he's able to work fully. Either way, with Travis Etienne -- who recorded 260 carries in 17 regular-season games in 2025 -- no longer in the mix, Tuten's role is destined to expand in 2026,…

items.h: Jaguars head coach Liam Coen said Wednesday in an appearance on "The Schrager Hour" podcast that he's "definitely expecting Tuten to have a big year" after the running back had "a really good spring."
items.s: Coen's comments only add to the buzz surrounding Tuten heading into training camp, as the second-year back had already been expected to see an enhanced profile in the Jacksonville offense in 2026 after the team let Travis Etienne walk in free agency. As a rookie, Tuten produced seven touchdowns on 93 touches while mainly serving as a short-yardage complement to Etienne, but the 23-year-old ran a 4.32-second 40-yard dash in the pre-draft process and put that explosiveness on display in the Jaguars' playoff loss to the Bills, reeling off three runs for 10-plus yards. The extent to which…

items.h: In the wake of the offseason departure of Travis Etienne, John Shipley of SI.com notes that "all signs point" to the Jaguars employing a timeshare backfield led by Tuten and Chris Rodriguez (foot).
items.s: LeQuint Allen will also mix in to some degree, but there's likely to be a heated battle between Tuten - who's coming off a strong offseason program -- and Rodriguez (who is bouncing back from a foot procedure) for the top spot during training camp, and coach Liam Coen has referred to the situation as "truly wide open." Tuten's upside as a pass-catcher could give him a narrow edge over Rodriguez when it comes to touch and snap volume, but this is a looming committee situation from a fantasy perspective.

items.h: With Chris Rodriguez recovering from a foot procedure, Tuten and LeQuint Allen took the majority of the Jaguars' running back reps during OTAs and at Tuesday's mandatory minicamp session, Michael DiRocco of ESPN reports.
items.s: According to coach Liam Coen, Rodriguez "will be full go come training camp" after hurting his left foot at the beginning of the team's offseason conditioning program. Once he's back on the field, the free-agent addition is set to compete with Tuten and Allen for slotting in a backfield that no longer includes Travis Etienne. As a rookie last season, Tuten gained 307 yards and five TDs on 83 carries while adding 10 catches for 79 yards and a pair of receiving TDs in 15 regular-season contests. The 2025 fourth-rounder has an opportunity to carve a larger role this season, but Coen previously…

items.h: Tuten will likely see a similar workload to Chris Rodriguez as the leaders of Jacksonville's new-look backfield, John Shipley of SI.com reports.
items.s: Tuten finished second on the team in carries as a rookie during the regular season, as the 2025 fourth-round pick rushed 83 times for 307 yards and five touchdowns while working as the backup to Travis Etienne, who subsequently signed a four-year contract with the Saints in free agency. Jacksonville brought in Rodriguez on a two-year, $10-million contract but didn't draft any running backs, setting Tuten and Rodriguez up to split most of the carries ahead of passing-down specialists LeQuint Allen and DeeJay Dallas.

items.h: Tuten finished the 2025 season with 307 yards and five touchdowns on 83 rushing attempts. He also had 10 catches for 79 yards and two touchdowns in 15 regular-season games.
items.s: A finger injury kept Tuten out for two games in 2025. When available, the fourth-round rookie carried the ball in every game he appeared in during the season, with his most impactful game occurring in Week 11, when he had 15 attempts. Travis Etienne remained the starter for the entirety of the season, but he is expected to be an unrestricted free agent in March. Should Etienne leave, Tuten could have an opportunity for a larger role in 2026.

items.h: Tuten rushed five times for 23 yards and one touchdown in the Jaguars' 41-7 win over the Titans on Sunday.
items.s: Tuten carried the ball five times behind Travis Etienne's 14, but it was Tuten who scored a touchdown in this one, as he punched in a five-yard score in the fourth quarter of the blowout win. Tuten will handle RB2 duties behind Etienne for next weekend's wild-card matchup with the Bills.

items.h: Tuten (finger) is not listed on Wednesday's injury report.
items.s: Tuten has missed back-to-back games due to a lingering finger injury, but it looks as though he's fully on track to return as the top backup behind Travis Etienne for Sunday's regular-season finale against the Titans. Jacksonville can clinch the AFC South title with a victory at home against Tennessee on Sunday, and against the 3-13 Titans, there could be plenty of backfield production to go around.

items.h: Tuten (finger) has been downgraded to out for Sunday's game against the Colts.
items.s: Tuten was initially listed as questionable for Sunday's contest, but he'll need to spend at least one more game on the sideline while continuing to recover from his right finger injury. With Tuten having logged a trio of limited practice sessions in preparation, however, there's reason to be optimistic about his chances of retaking the field in time to suit up for Jacksonville's regular-season finale against the Titans in Week 18.

items.h: Tuten (finger) has been deemed questionable to play against Indianapolis on Sunday, Michael DiRocco of ESPN.com reports.
items.s: Tuten missed last Sunday's win over Denver due to a finger injury, but he was able to log a trio of limited practice sessions this week. That gives him a chance of suiting up Sunday, though his status may not be determined until Jacksonville releases its list of inactives approximately 90 minutes prior to the 1:00 p.m. ET kickoff. If Tuten can't play, LeQuint Allen and DeeJay Dallas would be the Jaguars' backfield options behind top tailback Travis Etienne.

items.h: Tuten (finger) was a limited participant in Thursday's practice.
items.s: Tuten was unable to suit up for Jacksonville's win over the Broncos in Week 16 due to a right finger issue that it was reported could sideline him multiple games, so it's encouraging to see him now log a second consecutive limited practice session. If Tuten is able to log at least another limited practice session Friday, it appears he'll have a fair chance to reclaim his No. 2 role behind Travis Etienne as early as Sunday on the road against Indianapolis.
